Audit and fix website accessibility issues focusing on shared layouts, reusable components, and key pages

  • Preview latest task
index.htmlHTML
Antonio Tesse

Audit this site for accessibility issues and fix them.

Pages to audit: {{PAGES}} Focus areas: {{FOCUS_AREAS}}

Start with shared layouts and reusable components — fixes there propagate to every page that uses them. Then check individual pages. If no pages are specified, audit the homepage and up to 5 other key pages (pages with forms, navigation, or interactive elements).

If focus areas are specified, prioritize those. Otherwise, check and fix all of the following:

Images: Add descriptive alt text to all <img> tags. Use alt="" for decorative images only. Form labels: Ensure every form input has an associated <label>. Add aria-label to icon-only buttons.

Heading hierarchy: Ensure one <h1> per page and no skipped levels (e.g., <h2> straight to <h4>).

ARIA attributes: Add missing role, aria-label, and aria-expanded attributes to interactive elements like menus, modals, and dropdowns.

Keyboard focus: Add visible focus styles (:focus-visible) to all interactive elements. Ensure modals and dropdowns trap focus when open.

Language: Add a lang attribute to the <html> tag if missing.

15 minutes ago
Claude Agent
A

The ONMEC Jannuzzi Racing website is now live as a static page, and it has been through a full accessibility audit with fixes applied. The site is a single bilingual page, so the shared pieces (header, navigation, mobile menu, footer) and every section were checked: hero, team, institute, municipality, the car and wind-tunnel simulator, milestones, sponsors and the contact form.

Shared layout and navigation. A "skip to main content" link and a <main> landmark now let keyboard and screen-reader users jump past the header. Both navigation menus have names, and the footer is labelled. The mobile menu button tells assistive technology whether the menu is open, swaps between a hamburger and a close icon, keeps keyboard focus inside the menu while it is open, closes with Escape and returns focus to the button. The Italian/English switch now updates the page's lang attribute, so screen readers change pronunciation with the language. The buttons report which language is active, and the flag emojis are no longer read aloud.

Keyboard focus. Every link, button, form field, tab and the speed slider now shows a clearly visible cyan focus outline when reached by keyboard. Before, form fields had their outline removed and most other controls had no visible focus at all.

Images and graphics. The team photo already had good alt text. The 106 decorative Font Awesome icons and the repeated emblem graphics are now hidden from screen readers, which used to announce them as noise. The two technical car illustrations got short descriptions. The decorative animated background is hidden from screen readers and stops animating for visitors who turn on reduced motion in their system settings.

Headings. The page keeps a single <h1>. Skipped levels were fixed: the component detail panel in the car section and the contact cards jumped from <h2> to <h4>, and the footer column titles were <h4> with no parent headings.

Interactive components. The team filters, simulator modes and component selector now report which option is selected. The season switcher was marked as a tab list but had no tabs inside it. It now works as proper tabs: the selected tab is announced, each tab is linked to its panel, and the arrow, Home and End keys move between tabs. Simulator readings, the component details, the "copy email" confirmation and the slider value (read as "78 km/h") are now announced as they change.

Contact form. Every field already had a visible label. The fields now have names, autofill hints for name, organisation and email, and are marked as required for assistive technology. After the form is sent, focus moves to the confirmation message so it gets announced.

Other fixes found along the way. Switching language erased the pulsing dot on the 2026/2027 tab, and after using the simulator buttons or component selector, switching language stopped updating those buttons' text. Both are fixed. The form's thank-you message now escapes whatever the visitor typed, so text typed into the form can no longer be inserted into the page as code.

Worth reviewing. The LinkedIn and YouTube icons in the footer only link back to the contact section. Pointing them at the real profiles, or removing them, would help every visitor. The hero introduction paragraph also ends mid-sentence ("…con il supporto e la sponsorizzazione del"), which looks like copy that still needs finishing.
